title: - Bhikkhus, if a bhikkhu reviles, criticizes, and scolds the noble ones and his fellow celibates, it is impossible, it cannot happen that he will…
content: - Bhikkhus, if a bhikkhu reviles, criticizes, and scolds the noble ones and his fellow celibates, it is impossible, it cannot happen that he will not encounter one of these ten misfortunes. What ten? He does not attain what has not been attained; what has been attained declines; he does not become well-versed in the good Dhamma; he becomes over-conceited regarding the good Dhamma; he does not live the holy life with joy; he commits a corrupt offense; he experiences a severe illness; he becomes mentally deranged; he becomes confused at the time of death; or after death, with the breakup of the body, he is reborn in a plane of misery, a bad destination, a lower realm, hell. Bhikkhus, if a bhikkhu reviles, criticizes, and scolds the noble ones and his fellow celibates, it is impossible, it cannot happen that he will not encounter one of these ten misfortunes.

title: Friends, if others should treat a bhikkhu who is not perfect, not good, not pleasant, by touching him with hands, with stones, with sticks, or…
content: Friends, if others should treat a bhikkhu who is not perfect, not good, not pleasant, by touching him with hands, with stones, with sticks, or with swords, he understands thus: 'Such is the nature of this body that hands can touch it, stones can touch it, sticks can touch it, swords can touch it. The Blessed One has said in the simile of the saw: "Bhikkhus, even if low-down bandits were to saw your limbs one by one with a two-handled saw, yet if anyone among you defiled his mind, that person would not be following my teaching." I will be energetic and diligent, not lazy. Mindfulness is established without confusion, my body is tranquil, not agitated, my mind is concentrated and unified. Now let hands touch this body, let stones touch this body, let sticks touch this body, let swords touch this body — the teaching of the Buddhas must be practiced.'

title: Householder, that noble disciple, having known that sensual desire is a defilement of the mind, abandons sensual desire, the defilement of the mind; having known…
content: Householder, that noble disciple, having known that sensual desire is a defilement of the mind, abandons sensual desire, the defilement of the mind; having known that hatred is a defilement of the mind, abandons hatred, the defilement of the mind; having known that dullness and drowsiness are defilements of the mind, abandons dullness and drowsiness, the defilements of the mind; having known that restlessness and remorse are defilements of the mind, abandons restlessness and remorse, the defilements of the mind; having known that doubt is a defilement of the mind, abandons doubt, the defilement of the mind. This, householder, is called a noble disciple of great wisdom, of wide wisdom, one who has entered the domain of clear vision, possessed of wisdom. This is called being complete in wisdom.

title: Craving, bhikkhus, is a net that makes the wandering in saṃsāra spread out, sticky; it is because of that craving that this world is destroyed,…
content: Craving, bhikkhus, is a net that makes the wandering in saṃsāra spread out, sticky; it is because of that craving that this world is destroyed, bound, tangled like a ball of thread, like a matted cocoon, like twisted muñja grass and babhaja reeds, unable to escape from the plane of misery, the bad destination, the lower realm, birth and death.

title: Sātāgira: The sage's mind is fully accomplished, His deeds are perfectly done. Let us approach the Venerable Gotama, Fully possessed of wisdom and good conduct.…
content:
Sātāgira:
The sage's mind is fully accomplished,
His deeds are perfectly done.
Let us approach the Venerable Gotama,
Fully possessed of wisdom and good conduct.

Hemāvata:
His calves are like an antelope's, lean and steady,
With little food, not greedy, absorbed in jhāna.
Let us go and see the seer Gotama
Who practices jhāna in the remote forest.

Alone, like a lion, like an elephant, not grasping at pleasures,
Let us approach and ask him about release from the snare of death.

title: Bhikkhus, there are these five benefits for a patient person. What five? People love him and like him; no one hates him; not many people…
content: Bhikkhus, there are these five benefits for a patient person. What five? People love him and like him; no one hates him; not many people avoid him; at the time of death his mind is not confused; after death, with the breakup of the body, he is reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world. Bhikkhus, these are the five benefits for a patient person.

title: 'For what reason, friends, for what condition does unarisen greed not arise, or arisen greed is abandoned?' The answer should be: 'The sign of the…
content: 'For what reason, friends, for what condition does unarisen greed not arise, or arisen greed is abandoned?' The answer should be: 'The sign of the foul.' For one who gives wise attention to the sign of the foul, unarisen greed does not arise, and arisen greed is abandoned. This, friends, is the cause, this is the condition for the non-arising of unarisen greed and for the abandoning of arisen greed.' 'For what reason, friends, for what condition does unarisen hatred not arise, or arisen hatred is abandoned?' The answer should be: 'The liberation of mind by loving-kindness.' For one who gives wise attention to the liberation of mind by loving-kindness, unarisen hatred does not arise, and arisen hatred is abandoned. This, friends, is the cause, this is the condition for the non-arising of unarisen hatred and for the abandoning of arisen hatred.' 'For what reason, friends, for what condition does unarisen delusion not arise, or arisen delusion is abandoned?' The answer should be: 'Wise attention.' For one who gives wise attention, unarisen delusion does not arise, and arisen delusion is abandoned. This, friends, is the cause, this is the condition for the non-arising of unarisen delusion and for the abandoning of arisen delusion.'

title: Bhikkhus, an unlearned ordinary person does not truly understand the arising, the passing away, the gratification, the danger, and the escape of form. Of feeling…
content: Bhikkhus, an unlearned ordinary person does not truly understand the arising, the passing away, the gratification, the danger, and the escape of form. Of feeling ... of perception ... of formations ... He does not truly understand the arising, the passing away, the gratification, the danger, and the escape of consciousness. Bhikkhus, a learned noble disciple truly understands the arising, the passing away, the gratification, the danger, and the escape of form. Of feeling ... of perception ... of formations ... He truly understands the arising, the passing away, the gratification, the danger, and the escape of consciousness.

title: Young householder, keeping bad company has six dangers: gamblers, libertines, drunkards, swindlers, deceivers, and violent persons are his friends and companions. Young householder, such are…
content: Young householder, keeping bad company has six dangers: gamblers, libertines, drunkards, swindlers, deceivers, and violent persons are his friends and companions. Young householder, such are the six dangers of keeping bad company.

title: Bhikkhus, how does a bhikkhu have increase of wealth? Bhikkhus, here a bhikkhu abides pervading one direction with a mind imbued with loving-kindness, likewise the…
content: Bhikkhus, how does a bhikkhu have increase of wealth? Bhikkhus, here a bhikkhu abides pervading one direction with a mind imbued with loving-kindness, likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth. Thus above, below, across, everywhere, in all respects, he abides pervading the entire world with a mind imbued with loving-kindness, vast, immeasurable, without hostility, without ill-will. He abides pervading with a mind imbued with compassion ... with a mind imbued with altruistic joy ... He abides pervading with a mind imbued with equanimity, vast, immeasurable, without hostility, without ill-will. Bhikkhus, thus a bhikkhu has increase of wealth.
